newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SOCCER-LATE MILOSEVIC GOAL GIVES YUGOSLAVIA VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LATE MILOSEVIC GOAL GIVES YUGOSLAVIA VICTORY.

text.p: Two late substitutes combined to give Yugoslavia a 2-1 victory over the Czech Republic in their European group six qualifier on Wednesday, all but ending the Czech's hopes of a spot in the 1998 World Cup finals.

Aston Villa's Savo Milosevic, who came on for AC Milan's Dejan Savicevic in the 82nd minute, took substitute Ljubinko Drulovic's cross and found the back of the net in the final minute to give the Yugoslavs victory -- despite being outplayed for much of the game.
Yugoslavia move on to 15 points from six matches, one fewer than group leaders Spain who have played the same number of games. Slovakia are third on 12 points, followed by the Czechs on four.
"Now we will have to work for a miracle," said Kaiserslautern striker Pavel Kuka, who missed several good scoring chances for the Czechs.

The Czechs, beaten Euro 96 finalists, dominated play from the opening whistle but failed to find the scoring touch that has deserted them since opening the qualifying round with a 6-0 drubbing of Malta.

Kuka, Vladimir Smicer and Karel Poborsky all sneaked past the Yugoslav defence in the first half for clear shots on goal from inside the penalty box, only to shoot straight at Yugoslav keeper Ivica Kralj.

Meanwhile, Yugoslavia attacked sparingly but made their best chance count when Predrag Mijatovic bent a free kick from just outside the box around the Czech wall and into the near corner in the 28th minute.

The Czechs, who controlled the ball for nearly 60 per cent of the game, finally broke through the Yugoslav defence when Radek Bejbl picked up a loose ball in front of the box, driving his shot past a helpless Kralj.

But Bejbl's goal gave the sold-out Letna Stadium crowd something to cheer about for only 15 minutes, before Drulovic, who substitued in the 86th minute and barely missed the mark himself just seconds earlier found the streaking Milosevic.
"We had our chances and could have scored several goals, but they just didn't go in. It's tough to lose like that," said Czech coach Dusan Uhrin.

Added Yugoslav coach Slobodan Santrac: "In this situation, when you win against such a difficult opponent, it's hard to find words. The football world will really lose out when one of these teams don't make it to France."
